sections.title: AI security & GRC
sections.subtitle: Test AI risks, apply guardrails and turn control gaps into audit-ready evidence.

sections.heading: From AI security risk to accountable controls
sections.body:
Connect AI and LLM test findings with guardrails, control owners and remediation evidence. Agree which systems, data and requirements are in scope before assessment. Start when AI adoption outpaces control ownership or an assurance review needs traceable evidence.

Infrastructure and identity controls belong to [Cloud security & IAM](/services/cyber-security/cloud-security-iam); web, code and supply-chain testing to [Exposure validation & AppSec](/services/cyber-security/exposure-validation-appsec). For enterprise AI policy and roadmaps, see [AI strategy & governance](/services/data-ai/ai-strategy-governance).

sections.heading: Requirements, controls and reviewable evidence
sections.description: Agree the applicable requirements with risk and legal owners before mapping controls. Assessment does not certify compliance or replace legal advice.

items.title: Data protection scope
items.description: Agree whether POPIA safeguards, operator arrangements and cross-border processing apply to the AI systems assessed.
items.bullets:
Control: data-access and handling decisions
Evidence: approved scope and owner record

items.title: Enterprise control mapping
items.description: Agree whether ISO/IEC 27001:2022 or NIST CSF 2.0 is the relevant mapping basis; ISO control mapping is not certification.
items.bullets:
Control: requirement-to-owner mapping
Evidence: control matrix and gap status

items.title: AI testing and oversight
items.description: Confirm applicable OWASP AI/LLM guidance and any ISO/IEC 42001 mapping before including them in the assessment.
items.bullets:
Control: agreed tests and human sign-off
Evidence: findings, changes and retest record

sections.heading: Scope the assessment and engagement
sections.description: The next step is a scoping discussion about AI systems, control objectives and the evidence you need. Do not send credentials, personal information or confidential test findings.

items.title: What do we need to begin?
items.description: An inventory of the AI systems and data categories, accountable owners, assessment objectives and authorised access. Agree test-data handling, legal requirements and the secure exchange process before sharing confidential material.

items.title: What does the evidence pack contain?
items.description: The agreed scope, test scenarios, findings and limitations, control-owner-evidence matrix, remediation decisions and retest status. Define the review cadence and sign-off criteria at the start.

items.title: How can we buy the work?
items.description: Fixed Price suits a defined assessment with agreed acceptance criteria; Time & Materials suits evolving discovery. An ongoing Managed Service, Dedicated Team or Outcome-Based scope can be considered where responsibilities and measurable acceptance can be agreed. Explore our [commercial models](/company/our-approach#engagement-models). Product licensing is separate.

items.title: Is this certification or an AI roadmap?
items.description: No. Assessment and control mapping support evidence readiness; they do not certify compliance or replace legal advice. Enterprise AI policy and roadmaps are a separate [AI strategy & governance](/services/data-ai/ai-strategy-governance) scope. We can agree an NDA before reviewing confidential material; read our [privacy policy](/privacy-policy) before enquiring.
